key_insight: Paint-Anything shows that any-color control can be unified for both image generation and editing by learning a shared representation for hex color values. This lets users specify exact 24-bit colors more naturally, without relying on specialized color-only pipelines.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of precisely controlling object colors in image generation and editing using arbitrary hex codes. Existing methods often need custom color representations or special inference steps, which makes them less flexible and harder to use in real design workflows.
method: Learn a shared mapping between hex color values and color semantics so the model can understand exact user-specified colors.
Support both image generation and image editing under one unified any-color control framework.
Leverage large language model capabilities to interpret compact color codes without requiring dedicated color-specific procedures.
impact: This makes color control more practical for designers and AI practitioners who need exact, reproducible color specification. It simplifies workflows and expands the usability of generative models for professional visual design tasks.

paper_title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
paper_authors: Ji Xie, Dewei Zhou, Xinyu Huang, Zhennan Chen, Xun Wang
